messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO Alert: Canary pool (canary-us-west-2) p99 latency spike above 2.5s for 5m. Auto-pager triggered. Root: rollout traffic shift -> model v1.3-canary
sasha: I'm on it, paging oncall now. which canary size did we push? deploy-bot: Released v1.3-canary to canary-us-west-2 with 12% traffic at 15:07 UTC
aj: seeing p95 ~800ms but p99 jumps to 3.1s and streaming stalls at tail. Multiplex queues growing on shards 4/7.
maria: logs show increased kv cache miss rate and some encoder packets hitting quantized path slow branch. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T15:09Z encoder: encode_latency p99=3100ms kv_miss=0.18 model=v1.3-canary
2026-03-15T15:09Z runtime: batch_queue_len=42 shard=4
```
kevin: can we shadow traffic away from canary? I can change routing to 0% but need approval for rollback.
anya: agreed. First live mitigation: reduce canary traffic to 0%, enable fallback to v1.2-stable, and increase autoscale concurrency cap for dedicated pool.
sasha: doing the traffic shift now — switching canary route to drained. aj: please confirm the gating config id.
aj: gating config is `route-2026-03-canary-13`. Running `rbac` change.
deploy-bot: Route update: canary-us-west-2 -> 0% at 15:12 UTC (initiated by sasha)
aj: traffic drained to 0% for canary pool, latency improving on p99 within samples but tail still sticky on some frontends.
maria: KV warmup doesn't look complete on a subset of workers — eviction churn for embeddings cache around that time. proposing cache pre-warm + replicated warm nodes.
kevin: immediate step: clear stale cache entries for affected shards and bump warmup parallelism. Running command:
```
infra-cli cache evict --shard 4 --pattern stale_* && infra-cli cache warmup --shard 4 --parallel 8
```
anya: doing cache evict/warmup on shard 4 and 5 now.
support-bot: customer-impact check: 21 requests in last 10m returned 504/timeouts from us-west region, no broad customer outage reported yet. list: customer-a (3), customer-b (2), internal-eval (16)
product-lead: flagging for triage with product — any visible degradation in embeddings endpoints or just generation/streaming?
aj: mostly streaming/generation. embeddings endpoints stable. Streaming stalls manifest as partial chunks then final delay.
maria: collecting runtime traces for stalled sessions. saving sample trace ids: trace-7751, trace-7752.
sasha: oncall-handoff: paging now. @oncall-bot can you take over live mitigation coordination? I'll stay for 1st handoff.
oncall-bot: @sasha acknowledged. Assigning incident to oncall SRE: kevin_sre. Severity: Sev2. Handoff channel: #incidents-oncall-handovers
kevin: I'm oncall and joined. what's current status summary?
sasha: canary traffic drained to 0%, fallback to v1.2-stable is active for affected routes, cache warmup in progress, p99 trending down from 3.1s to 1.8s over last 2 minutes. customer timeouts small but visible.
kevin: ok. next: monitor p99 for 15m, keep canary at 0%, prepare rollback plan for full rollout cancellation, and run canary post-mortem. any signs of model regression in smaller eval set?
anya: quick local eval shows slight increase in decode time for some sequences on v1.3, likely due to kernel selection falling back to non-quant fast-path for long prompts.
aj: will add a short-term runtime patch to prefer the alternate kernel for those prompt lengths. patch is low-risk, hotfix branch `runtime/favor-kern-A`.
maria: collecting perf counters and will attach to the incident doc. also noting that multiplex queueing and encoder stalls were correlated with a small spike of long-prompt requests around 15:05 UTC (sample id list attached in internal doc).
support-bot: opened incident ticket INC-2026-1842 and added customers affected. Notifying account teams for customers with >1 timeout.
product-lead: important to confirm whether this is strictly performance regression or correctness change. Schedule quick eval against canary samples.
kevin: decision: keep canary at 0%, abort the v1.3 rollout. no immediate rollback needed since we never fully shifted, but mark rollout as failed and block subsequent rollouts until root cause traced.
aj: I've gated the rollout in the control plane and set `rollout: aborted` for v1.3 in the deployment service.
deploy-bot: Rollout status: v1.3-canary -> aborted at 15:22 UTC
sasha: preparing postmortem skeleton, will include timeline, mitigation steps, and customer impact. assigning owners: runtime perf (aj), infra/cache (anya), oncall lead (kevin), product/evals (product-lead).
kevin: I'll own the immediate 2-hour bridge to ensure p99 stabilizes and follow-up with SRE rotation. handoff notes: monitor canary pool for accidental traffic, verify cache warmup successes for shards 4/5, validate kernel selection logs for replaced fallback.
anya: cache warmup completed on shard 4/5 at 15:25, eviction reduced churn. monitoring metric: kv_miss down to 0.04.
maria: attaching trace ids and perf graphs to INC-2026-1842.
support-bot: customer-impact summary: 21 total requests impacted, none escalated to SLAs breach at account level. support outreach started for customer-a and internal-eval.
product-lead: thanks team. we'll reconvene for a deep-dive tomorrow. for now, kevin will handle oncall bridge until 17:30 UTC. Sasha, please hand off any live dashboards you maintain.
sasha: handing over dashboard links and notes in #incidents-oncall-handovers. leaving the channel but will be available if needed. :white_check_mark:
kevin: acknowledged. Incident status: mitigation complete, canary aborted, monitoring ongoing. will update incident ticket with final notes and close when p99 stable for 30m.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1842 updated: status=mitigated, severity=Sev2, handlers=[kevin_sre, aj, anya, sasha].
